event.piper_heart2.1.text: Thumb there, two fingers there, now pull. ...There. Hear that? That's a D. It forgives everything.
event.piper_heart2.1.why: names the chord; 'it forgives everything' is warmer and truer than 'that's the whole secret'

event.piper_heart2.2.text: Here, a sunflower for your first gig. Don't quit the farm. Friday, chord two. It's the honest one.
event.piper_heart2.2.why: pairs 'the friendly one' with 'the honest one'; the Friday promise is the thread

event.piper_heart5.1.text: First time out of the case. Even Elara hasn't heard it, and her needles always get the first verse.
event.piper_heart5.1.why: the needles-keep-time detail makes skipping Elara land as the gift it is

event.piper_heart5.3.text: If it's bad, clap anyway. If it's good, don't clap. Hum it tomorrow where I can hear.
event.piper_heart5.3.why: plants her real want (being hummed without her) instead of a generic clap joke

event.piper_heart5.2.text: It ends on four notes I hum when nobody's around. I never wrote them. They were just... in my hands.
event.piper_heart5.2.why: 'I never wrote them' is stranger and truer than 'I keep meaning to find out'

dlg.story.umbrella.talk.1.text: Third escape this season. It always turns up hung neatly, drier than I am. What do we do?
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.1.why: 'hung neatly' seeds the mystery before the choice, so every branch pays it

dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r1.text: Leave it? ...All right. Red reads loud in the rain, and somebody out there needs loud.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r1.why: 'needs loud' is her shape of generosity; funniest word last

event.story_umbrella.after.text: {if choice:umbrella.return}Back where it belongs. But someone keeps hanging it up so neatly. Who tidies a stranger's umbrella?{else}{if choice:umbrella.hang}A landmark. I'll check it every rain. And I'll find out who hangs it so neatly. They fold the ribbon.{else}Shared custody. I accept, under protest. Bring it Fridays so it hears me play.{/if}{/if}
event.story_umbrella.after.why: the hang branch now carries the neat-hanger mystery too; 'they fold the ribbon' is the noticing

event.piper_heart4.intro.text: Last set tonight, and it's yours. Request anything. For once I'll even play it.
event.piper_heart4.intro.why: self-callback to her standing joke ('I'll probably play something else') turned inside out for the player

dlg.piper.fright.0.text: A hundred people, no blinking, every Friday. Tonight they'll notice the trick. The playing's real. The rest is volume.
dlg.piper.fright.0.why: 'the rest is volume' confesses the mechanism, not just the feeling

dlg.piper.fright.r1.text: ...You didn't fill it. I always fill it. That's the job, I thought. ...Quiet's not so loud with two.
dlg.piper.fright.r1.why: old line blamed others for filling her quiet; it was always her job, and that's the confession

event.piper_heart6.after.text: The nerves are coming upstairs with me, just smaller. They fit in the fiddle case, next to the rosin. Someday I want a song they sing without me. Tonight, I'll settle for the stairs.
event.piper_heart6.after.why: 'next to the rosin' brushes Hazel's hiding spot without knowing it; the deflate ends it

event.piper_heart8.intro.text: Sit by the stage. I'm writing a new one, and I'm not doing it alone this time. Alone is how you end up rhyming 'parsnip'.
event.piper_heart8.intro.why: self-aware parsnip callback says why she needs the player without saying it

dlg.piper.chorus.r0.text: Home. ...Oh. Three months I've been circling that word. It just walked in and sat down.
dlg.piper.chorus.r0.why: 'walked in and sat down' is the player, said sideways

dlg.piper.chorus.r1.text: The road. Wide and honest, and it rhymes with 'showed'. Too neatly. I don't trust a clean rhyme.
dlg.piper.chorus.r1.why: 'code' was not a village word; distrusting a clean rhyme is a fresh turn on her bit

event.piper_heart10.req_ballad.text: You asked for a ballad once. I wrote it down and said it mattered later. This is later. The sad middle is yours.
event.piper_heart10.req_ballad.why: pays the exact promise from heart 4 ('it matters later') word for word

event.piper_heart10.req_jig.text: You asked for a jig once. I said don't ask why yet. The last verse is why. Watch the floor.
event.piper_heart10.req_jig.why: pays the heart 4 promise ('don't ask why yet')

event.piper_heart10.req_parsnip.text: I said I'd play your request back someday. Listen to the second verse. There's a parsnip in it. Nobody's ever caught it.
event.piper_heart10.req_parsnip.why: pays the heart 4 promise ('someday I'll play it back')

event.piper_friend.intro.text: Friday! The parsnip ballad, all four verses. One's about the gray cat. I call it Sharp. It has notes.
event.piper_friend.intro.why: uses her shipped name for the cat; 'it has notes' is the pun she'd make

event.piper_friend.doing.text: 'Oh parsnip, pale and patient root...' and then 'pulled up early, absolute.' It rhymes if you squint. Squint harder.
event.piper_friend.doing.why: root/boot rhymed too well for the bit; root/absolute is properly off, and 'squint harder' owns it

event.piper_birthday.intro.text: My birthday! I wrote myself a song, since I know exactly what I like. It's a modest masterpiece.
event.piper_birthday.intro.why: vain-then-deflate in one breath; sharper reason to write her own birthday song

event.piper_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.piper.wish}Your wish made the encore. I rhymed 'birthday' with 'worth the day'. Don't check.{else}{if choice:bday.piper.sing}My song in your voice. The room clapped for you, and I just stood there, grinning like a lantern.{else}A song's coming with your name in it. Don't ask when. It will rhyme. Eventually.{/if}{/if}
event.piper_birthday.after.why: old sing branch said 'jealous', which fights her core want; hearing it sung is pure joy

event.piper_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.piper.song}Your name's in the bridge. The bridge is the best part. That's not an accident.{else}{if choice:courtship.piper.duet}We sang the chorus together, and the room came in behind us. I forgot to play for a bar. Worth it.{else}A walk home under the stars. I hummed. You hummed back. Best accompaniment I've ever had.{/if}{/if}
event.piper_partners.after.why: duet branch: forgetting to play for a bar beats nearly forgetting the bridge; the want, lived

event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l4.text: Pencil, then. Whoever fixes my rhymes can fix that one too. Save me the last glass.
event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l4.why: old 'fixing my pencil' read as pencil repair; now it points cleanly at the neat-pencil rhyme-fixer

event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l4.text: Deal! ...Make it a duet. You wrote one verse already. Write the second.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l4.why: calls back Wren's verse from 'The Shared Verse' instead of a vague 'your song too'

event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l3.text: My slow verse has a backbeat now! I felt it in my teeth!
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l3.why: the complaint is musical, which is how Piper complains

event.overheard_hazel_piper_1.l3.text: It was you! 'Spoon' is out, 'soon' is in, and the line's better. The best rhyme and it isn't mine!
event.overheard_hazel_piper_1.l3.why: 'the best rhyme and it isn't mine' touches her fear without naming it, and rhymes, barely

event.overheard_hazel_piper_2.l3.text: ...'Really' is gone. It scans! Hazel, where did you learn songs?
event.overheard_hazel_piper_2.l3.why: shows the fix landing before the question, so the question carries the awe

adds.text: Again. ...Once more. There, you've got it. The fiddle likes you. Don't be flattered. It's a shameless flirt.
adds.why: a beat of the player actually practicing, so her 'took me a week' sting has something to land on

adds.text: I skipped the skeleton too. Tuesdays I play new songs to the clinic skeleton. It never claps. Very honest audience.
adds.why: her Tuesday skeleton ritual from the bible, skipped for the player; funny and measures the gift

threads.piper_heart2: Friday and the second chord: if the first one was the friendly one, what does the honest one sound like?
threads.piper_heart5: The song ends on four notes she hums alone and never wrote; where did her hands learn them?
threads.story_umbrella: Someone keeps hanging the runaway umbrella up neatly, ribbon folded; who tidies a stranger's umbrella?
threads.story_band_battle: Bram tapped his foot on the second verse and will deny it until spring; what does a fiddle tune mean to him?
threads.piper_heart4: She wrote the request down and said it matters later; the player waits to find out when 'later' is.
threads.piper_heart6: She said the want out loud: a song they sing without her; the nerves go upstairs with her either way.
threads.piper_heart8: The chorus is finished; now it needs a room full of people to sing it without her.
threads.piper_heart10: They sang without her and she loved the quiet; what does she write now that the fear has nothing to eat?
threads.piper_friend: Verse five of the parsnip ballad, next Friday, is about the player.
threads.piper_birthday: A song with the player's name in it is coming, unfinished, on a musician's schedule.
threads.piper_courtship: The love song stays in the case, rhymed and bridged, with the last line left open.
threads.piper_courtship2: The second verse exists whatever the answer was; the last line is still waiting for its word.
threads.piper_partners: The first song she didn't hide behind a joke; the player wonders what else comes out of hiding.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_1: Friday's bridge goes up a key out of spite; the good stool keeps its opinions.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_2: Wren's verse will open Piper's next set, credit in tiny letters, huge feelings.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_3: Somebody neat keeps fixing her pencil rhymes, and Piper still hasn't caught them at it.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_4: The headline night wants to be a duet; Wren owes the second verse.

notes: piper_heart10's three req_* lines now pay off the exact promises in piper_heart4.after ('it matters later', 'don't ask why yet', 'play it back someday'); if heart 4 is retouched, keep those three phrases or retune heart 10 with them.

piper_heart6.after says the nerves fit in the case 'next to the rosin' — the rosin is where Hazel's hidden verse lives (overheard_hazel_piper_3). Piper doesn't know; it's a deliberate unknowing brush, cozy-safe. Flag it to Hazel's pass so she can enjoy it.

piper_birthday.after's sing branch said she was 'a tiny bit jealous' of the room singing; that contradicts her core want, so it's now pure joy. Also: hall_dance's chorus 'wherever the lamp is on' leans on Tilda's lamp — confirm Tilda's pass keeps the lamp.

Kept unchanged on purpose: both hall_dance lines, all of story_band_battle, the heart 6 choices and talk branch, heart 10 intro and outro, and the courtship trio — I couldn't beat them without making them busier.
